description: Mission Valdocco is a Costa Rican team uniting two award-winning agritech projects: AgroTico Smart, winner of Samsung Solve for Tomorrow LATAM 2025, a smart station with IoT sensors, NASA satellite data and AI to guide farmers; and INCUBiO, two-time ExpoSTEAM champion, an automated seed germinator.
summary:
Mission Valdocco is a web platform that helps farmers in Costa Rica make better planting decisions under an increasingly unpredictable climate. Droughts, out-of-season rains and heat waves cause heavy crop losses, and most farmers lack precise data about their own soil and microclimate. As a result, key decisions are often based on tradition or general forecasts that are no longer reliable.
Our platform uses artificial intelligence to combine NASA open data (SMAP, ECOSTRESS, GPM, Landsat, MODIS, NASA POWER, GRACE and GRACE-FO, and SRTM or other NASA elevation products) with Microsoft Planetary Computer, the Meteomatics Weather API, and readings from an on-site sensor station. The result is a clear, real-time report for each farm: which crops are most viable, when to plant them, and how to optimize water and fertilizer use. Farmers access everything through a web interface designed to be friendly and easy to use.
The system is modular, low-cost and energy-efficient, so it can be replicated in rural areas with limited resources. It automates data collection and analysis while keeping farmers in control of every decision, and its rollout includes training local technicians to close the technology gap in the field.
This matters because a failed harvest can cost a family its entire investment and income. By putting precision agriculture within reach of every farmer, Mission Valdocco reduces losses, strengthens food security, and contributes to the Sustainable Development Goals.
details:
Mission Valdocco

Making Local Sensor Readings and Earth Observation Data Easier for Farmers to Understand

Mission Valdocco is an agricultural monitoring project developed by a Costa Rican team for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Building on our previous project, AgroTico Smart, Mission Valdocco combines a physical environmental monitoring station with a web-based platform that integrates local sensor measurements, NASA Earth observation data, historical climate information, satellite imagery, and weather forecasts.

Our mission is to make complex environmental information accessible and understandable to farmers, helping them make more informed decisions about their crops and agricultural activities.

What Does the Project Do and How Does It Work?

Mission Valdocco connects three main sources of information: measurements collected directly in the field, satellite-based Earth observations, and weather forecasts.

  1. Local Environmental Monitoring: A Raspberry Pi-based agricultural station, equipped with environmental sensors, collects information about temperature, atmospheric pressure, humidity, CO₂ concentration, ultraviolet radiation, light intensity, and soil conditions. The readings are stored in a MySQL database and made available to the web application.
  2. NASA Earth Observation Integration: The platform incorporates NASA datasets and services to provide a broader understanding of environmental and agricultural conditions. These include NASA POWER for historical climate information, SMAP for soil moisture observations, ECOSTRESS for land surface temperature, GPM IMERG for precipitation, Landsat and HLS for land and vegetation observations, MODIS for vegetation indices, GRACE and GRACE-FO for regional water storage variations, and SRTM/NASADEM for elevation and terrain information.
  3. Satellite Imagery and Weather Forecasts: Microsoft Planetary Computer provides access to Sentinel-2 satellite imagery, allowing users to explore historical images of their surroundings. Meteomatics provides weather forecasts and visualization tools to help users understand possible upcoming weather conditions.
  4. An Accessible Agricultural Dashboard: The web application presents the information through an intuitive interface called Mi finca. Farmers can explore temperature, rainfall, wind, soil conditions, satellite imagery, historical records, and forecasts through visual indicators, interactive maps, charts, and simple descriptions.
  5. AI-Powered Agricultural Assistant: Mission Valdocco includes an AI assistant named Valdocco, powered by DeepSeek and integrated through the Vercel AI SDK. It uses the information available in the platform to answer questions in Spanish, explain environmental conditions, and help users understand the data without requiring advanced technical knowledge.

What Benefits Does the Project Have?

Mission Valdocco brings together different sources of agricultural and environmental information in a single platform, reducing the need to navigate multiple technical services and interpret complex datasets independently.

Its main benefits include:

  • Centralized information: Combines local sensor readings, satellite observations, historical climate information, and weather forecasts.
  • Better environmental awareness: Helps farmers understand changing weather conditions and environmental patterns around their farms.
  • Accessible technology: Presents complex scientific information through an interface designed for users with different levels of technological experience.
  • Historical analysis: Allows users to explore environmental trends and compare available measurements over time.
  • Satellite-based insights: Makes Earth observation information more approachable and provides additional context about soil moisture, vegetation, precipitation, surface temperature, and terrain.
  • AI-assisted understanding: Allows farmers to ask questions in natural Spanish and receive explanations based on the information available in the platform.

What Is the Intended Impact of the Project?

Our goal is to help small and medium-sized farmers, particularly in Costa Rica and other agricultural communities across Latin America, gain easier access to environmental information that can support their daily activities.

Agriculture is increasingly affected by changing weather patterns, irregular rainfall, temperature variations, and other environmental challenges. However, many farmers do not have access to tools that translate scientific and satellite data into practical information.

Mission Valdocco aims to bridge this gap by connecting technology developed for scientific observation with the real needs of agricultural communities.

By making environmental information easier to understand, the project seeks to support better-informed decisions regarding crop monitoring, agricultural planning, and resource management.

The platform is designed as a decision-support tool. It does not replace professional agronomic advice, direct field inspections, or farmers' experience. Instead, it provides additional information that can complement their knowledge.

Our long-term vision is to make accessible agricultural monitoring technology available to more communities, helping farmers better understand their environment and adapt to changing climatic conditions.

What Technologies, Hardware, and Software Did We Use?

Mission Valdocco combines hardware engineering, software development, artificial intelligence, satellite data processing, and cloud technologies.

Hardware and Sensors

  • Raspberry Pi: Main computing platform for the physical agricultural monitoring station.
  • BMP390: Atmospheric pressure and temperature measurements.
  • SCD30: CO₂ concentration, temperature, and relative humidity measurements.
  • LTR390: Ultraviolet radiation and ambient light measurements.
  • Soil moisture and soil temperature sensors: Monitoring of soil conditions.
  • GPS/location module: Geographic information associated with the monitoring station.

Programming Languages and Software Development

  • TypeScript and JavaScript: Main web application development.
  • Python: Hardware integration, sensor communication, and scientific data processing.
  • SQL: Database queries and data management.
  • HTML and CSS: Web interface structure and styling.
  • Next.js and React: Web application architecture and interactive user interface.
  • Tailwind CSS and Radix UI: Responsive design and interface components.
  • Recharts and Chart.js: Environmental data visualization.
  • MySQL: Storage and retrieval of monitoring station measurements.

NASA and Earth Observation Technologies

  • NASA POWER.
  • NASA Earthdata Common Metadata Repository (CMR).
  • NASA Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS).
  • SMAP, ECOSTRESS, GPM IMERG, Landsat, HLS, MODIS, GRACE, GRACE-FO, SRTM, and NASADEM datasets.
  • Microsoft Planetary Computer and Sentinel-2 satellite imagery.

Weather, Mapping, and Artificial Intelligence

  • Meteomatics API for weather forecasts and visualization.
  • Google Maps for geographic visualization.
  • OpenTopoData for elevation information.
  • DeepSeek API and Vercel AI SDK for the conversational AI assistant.

How Is the Project Creative and Innovative?

The creativity of Mission Valdocco lies in combining technologies that traditionally operate independently into a unified agricultural monitoring experience.

Instead of presenting farmers with isolated sensor measurements, complex satellite images, or scientific datasets, our platform connects these sources to provide a more complete environmental perspective.

One of our main innovations is the combination of a physical monitoring station with large-scale Earth observation data. Local sensors provide measurements close to the monitored area, while NASA datasets offer broader environmental context. Weather forecasts add a forward-looking perspective, helping users explore possible future conditions.

Another important creative element is the integration of an AI assistant specifically designed to explain available environmental information in everyday Spanish. Rather than requiring farmers to understand technical terminology, the assistant allows them to interact with the platform through natural questions.

We also designed two complementary experiences: a simplified interface for farmers, focused on clarity and accessibility, and a technical interface for users who want to explore detailed measurements, historical records, and scientific data.

This combination transforms complex environmental information into a more approachable and interactive experience.

What Factors Did Our Team Consider?

Throughout development, our team considered several technical, environmental, and social factors:

  • Accessibility: The platform needed to be understandable for farmers with different levels of digital literacy.
  • Data reliability: We considered the differences between local sensor measurements, satellite observations, historical climate datasets, and weather forecasts.
  • Spatial resolution: Some satellite products cover areas much larger than an individual farm, so their measurements must be interpreted with appropriate limitations.
  • Data availability: Satellite imagery can be affected by cloud cover, while some scientific products have publication delays or limited geographic coverage.
  • Sensor calibration: Physical sensor readings, especially soil moisture measurements, require proper calibration before being interpreted as definitive agricultural indicators.
  • Environmental relevance: We selected data sources that provide complementary information about temperature, precipitation, soil moisture, vegetation, water availability, and terrain.
  • Connectivity and infrastructure: The physical station and web application depend on reliable communication and access to external data services.
  • Responsible use of artificial intelligence: The AI assistant is intended to explain available information, not to provide unsupported diagnoses or make automatic agricultural decisions.
  • Scalability: We considered how the platform could evolve to support additional monitoring stations, agricultural areas, and environmental datasets.

Project Background and Team Vision

Mission Valdocco is an evolution of AgroTico Smart, our previous agricultural technology project developed in Costa Rica. It builds upon the experience and physical monitoring infrastructure developed through that initiative, expanding its capabilities through NASA Earth observation resources, satellite imagery, weather services, and artificial intelligence.

Our team brings together knowledge and experience in software development, electronics, electromechanical engineering, mechanical design, and data science.

We believe that technology should not only collect information but also make it useful to the people who need it most.

Mission Valdocco represents our vision of connecting Earth observation, artificial intelligence, and local innovation to help build a more informed, accessible, and resilient agricultural future.
